name: arm8-multiorgan
title: Arm 8 — Multi-organ scaling (where monolithic Tellurium strains)
question: As an SBML model grows large (tens -> hundreds -> thousands of species), where does a monolithic libroadrunner/CVODE instance strain — in model BUILD (compile) time, in integration time, or both — and does decomposing the body into N per-organ process-bigraph sub-processes coupled through a shared store actually come out ahead end-to-end, or does it just move the cost around?
hypothesis: A synthetic N-organ body (each organ a small 3-species chain, all coupled through one shared blood pool; species=3N+1, reactions=4N) run as ONE Antimony/Tellurium model will show the libroadrunner model build (compile) growing superlinearly in the reaction count and the dense CVODE step growing superlinearly in species. Decomposing into N per-organ libroadrunner instances coupled additively through a shared blood store (arm-3 pattern) replaces the one superlinear compile with N small ones, but adds per-tick orchestration overhead — so whether decomposition wins is an END-TO-END question, not a build-only one, and the answer depends on N and on the coupling interval that controls accuracy.
objective: Add a synthetic scaling knob (N organs) that stretches Tellurium past the fixed 17-species glycolysis model, and measure the HONEST end-to-end strain curve — monolithic build+run vs decomposed build+run — to locate where the monolith strains and to characterise, without overclaiming, when (if) decomposition comes out ahead.
description: Methods arm of the SBML-decomposition investigation. A synthetic multi-organ "body" is the scaling knob: N organ compartments, each a small 3-species enzymatic chain (o{i}_G -> o{i}_M -> o{i}_P), every one drawing from and returning to a SINGLE shared plasma metabolite Glc_blood (uptake + release flux), so the organs are genuinely coupled through the shared pool and the body is a closed, mass- conserving system that relaxes to a finite steady state at any N. Species = 3N+1, reactions = 4N. Two implementations run the SAME body: (1) MONOLITHIC — the whole N-organ model as one Antimony string integrated by a single libroadrunner/CVODE instance (build_multiorgan_antimony, on the generator's config.model so the Model page shows it); (2) DECOMPOSED — N OrganProcess nodes, each its own small libroadrunner instance built from that organ's 4 reactions, all sharing ONE blood store into which each writes its per-interval Glc_blood delta; the deltas reconcile additively through the bigraph apply path (exactly arm 3's shared-store coupling). multiorgan_scaling records, per N, BOTH halves of BOTH implementations — mono_build_s + mono_run_s (= mono_total_s) and decomp_build_s + decomp_run_s (= decomp_total_s) — plus accuracy (decomposed vs monolithic max_rel_err). The decomposed run is measured through N=128; N>=256 are build-only anchors (the decomposed pbg run is too slow for the harness there, and is left honestly unmeasured rather than guessed).
claim: The one strong, well-measured result is that the MONOLITHIC libroadrunner BUILD strains superlinearly in the reaction count: 0.20 s at 97 species -> 1.76 s at 385 -> 5.54 s at 769 -> 18.5 s at 1537 species (~94x for ~16x the reactions, ~O(N^1.64)), with the dense-CVODE run blowing up alongside it (0.0023 s -> 2.56 s). That is the real strain point and the reason a very large SBML model is painful to run monolithically. Decomposition is NOT a free win: building N small models is SLOWER than the single compile up to ~100 species (1.7x slower at 97 species), reaches only rough parity at 385 species (1.40 vs 1.76 s) and becomes a clear build win only at ~1500 species (2.4x); and the decomposed per-tick RUN overhead is ~16x the monolith's CVODE run, so the decomposed body is SLOWER END-TO-END at every N measured (decomp_total 2.35 s vs mono_total 1.81 s at 385 species). The end-to-end gap narrows with N but the decomposed run is unmeasured past N=128, so no end-to-end crossover is claimed. Decomposition is a structural trade — it swaps the monolith's superlinear build for much higher run overhead — that would only pay off end-to-end on models larger than measured. CRUCIAL caveat: the additive-split accuracy is good only at small N / fine interval (max_rel_err 2e-3 at N=2, 1.2e-2 at N=8, 5.2e-2 at N=32) and is 0.31 (31%) at N=128 — so the regime where the speed gap narrows and the regime of acceptable accuracy do NOT co-occur at a fixed coupling interval. All numbers measured, not fabricated.

expected_behavior.name: arm8-monolith-build-strains-superlinearly
expected_behavior.observable: monolithic libroadrunner build (compile) wall-clock vs the species/reaction count (3N+1 species, 4N reactions), and the decomposed-vs-monolithic accuracy at the default coupling interval
expected_behavior.condition: the monolithic build time grows superlinearly with the reaction count (the strain signal), AND the decomposed body reproduces the monolithic reference within tolerance at small N / fine interval (max_rel_err < 0.03 at N=8, coupling interval 0.05), with the error shrinking as the interval shrinks. No decomposition speed win is asserted — it does not hold end-to-end at the N measured.
expected_behavior.rationale: a single libroadrunner model build is superlinear in reactions and its CVODE Jacobian is dense in species, so a monolith must strain as the model grows — that much is a clean, defensible measurement. Whether decomposition is worth it is an end-to-end trade-off (build saved vs run overhead added vs accuracy lost), not a given, so the behavior gates only the measured strain + small-N fidelity.

findings.summary: STRONG RESULT — the monolithic libroadrunner BUILD (compile) strains superlinearly: measured medians 0.20 s at 97 species, 1.76 s at 385, 5.54 s at 769, 18.5 s at 1537 species — ~94x the build cost for ~16x the reactions (~O(N^1.64)). The dense-CVODE integration blows up alongside it (0.0023 s -> 0.058 s -> 0.395 s -> 2.56 s). Both halves of the monolithic cost grow superlinearly; this is the real, well-measured strain point and the arm's headline.

HONEST NEGATIVE — decomposition does NOT build "several-fold faster by hundreds of species". The decomposed build is N separate libroadrunner setups: SLOWER than the single monolithic compile up to ~100 species (97 sp: 0.34 s vs 0.20 s, 1.7x slower), roughly at PARITY by 385 species (1.40 vs 1.76 s), and a clear win only at ~1500 species (7.75 vs 18.5 s, 2.4x). The build crossover is at the hundreds-of-species scale, not before.

HONEST NEGATIVE (end-to-end) — the decomposed per-tick RUN overhead dwarfs the monolith's raw CVODE run: at 385 species decomp_run 0.95 s vs mono_run 0.058 s (~16x). So the decomposed body is SLOWER END-TO-END at every N measured: mono_total vs decomp_total = 0.017 vs 0.044 s (N=2), 0.039 vs 0.143 (N=8), 0.200 vs 0.559 (N=32), 1.81 vs 2.35 (N=128). The end-to-end gap narrows as N grows (3.6x -> 1.3x), but the decomposed run is UNMEASURED past N=128 (too slow for the harness), so NO end-to-end crossover is claimed. Decomposition trades the monolith's superlinear build for higher run overhead; it would only pay off end-to-end on models larger than we measured.

The coupling is genuine: Glc_blood lives in ONE shared store and every organ writes the delta it produced on it, reconciled additively through the bigraph apply path (arm-3 pattern). The shared pool drains more as more organs are added (monotone in N — a test asserts 8 organs drain it below the 2-organ case), which is only possible if the organs genuinely share the pool (contrast arm 7's N INDEPENDENT monoliths).

CRUCIAL caveat — accuracy and speed do NOT line up. The decomposed-vs-monolithic max_rel_err is a first-order additive-split error: 2e-3 at N=2, 1.2e-2 at N=8, 5.2e-2 at N=32, 0.31 (31%) at N=128. It HALVES as the coupling interval halves (verified) and GROWS with coupling density (more organs competing for the one pool per interval). The N=128 point where the end-to-end gap is smallest is exactly where accuracy (0.31) is unusable — so the speed crossover regime and the acceptable-accuracy regime do not co-occur at a fixed interval. Restoring accuracy at large N needs a finer interval, which adds more ticks and makes the decomposed run even slower. This is why the study verdict is PARTIAL.

arm8-monolith-build-strains-superlinearl.detail: monolithic build superlinear (0.20 s@97sp -> 18.5 s@1537sp, ~O(N^1.64)) — the strain signal, measured; decomposed matches monolith within tolerance at small N (max_rel_err 1.2e-2 @ N=8, interval 0.05). No decomposition speed win asserted (none holds end-to-end at measured N).

caveats: The monolithic build superlinearity is the one strong, well-measured result; the broader "decompose it and it scales better" narrative is NOT supported by the measurements and is deliberately not claimed.

Decomposition is SLOWER end-to-end at every N measured (through N=128); the decomposed run past N=128 is unmeasured, so no end-to-end crossover is claimed — only a structural build-vs-run trade is characterised.

The speed crossover regime (large N, where the end-to-end gap narrows) and the acceptable-accuracy regime (small N / fine interval) do not co-occur at a fixed coupling interval; accuracy at N=128 is 0.31.
